title: Rural Broadband Protection Act of 2025

claims.claim: Requires the FCC to establish within 180 days a formal vetting process.
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this subsection, the Commission shall initiate a rulemaking proceeding to establish a vetting process for applicants for, and other recipients of, a new covered funding award
claims.note: Source sets the 180-day deadline to INITIATE a rulemaking, not to establish/finalize the vetting process; the analysis's own gaps[0] concedes there is no completion deadline. 'establish within 180 days' compresses initiate-rulemaking into completed-process.

claims.claim: Short-title section - citation name only; no substantive effect.
claims.sourceSpan: SECTION 1. <<NOTE: 47 USC 609 note.>> SHORT TITLE.

claims.claim: Amends Section 254 of the Communications Act of 1934 to require FCC to initiate rulemaking within 180 days establishing a vetting process for high-cost USF applicants.
claims.sourceSpan: Section 254 of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 254) is amended by adding at the end the following

claims.claim: Applies to any new high-cost USF funding for broadband deployment, including reverse competitive bidding.
claims.sourceSpan: any new offer of high-cost universal service program funding, including funding provided through a reverse competitive bidding mechanism provided under this section, for the deployment of a broadband-capable network

claims.claim: Applications submitted after rules are promulgated must meet the new standards.
claims.sourceSpan: an award of covered funding that is made based on an application submitted to the Commission on or after the date on which rules are promulgated under paragraph (2)

claims.claim: The FCC must evaluate applicants against its Digital Opportunity Data Collection technical standards.
claims.sourceSpan: including the technical standards adopted by the Commission in orders of the Commission relating to Establishing the Digital Opportunity Data Collection (WC Docket No. 19-195)

claims.claim: and against each applicant's history of compliance with FCC and other government broadband funding programs.
claims.sourceSpan: the applicant's history of complying with requirements in Commission and other government broadband deployment funding programs

claims.claim: Sets a minimum pre-authorization default penalty of $9,000 per violation, with a base forfeiture floor of 30% of the applicant's total support.
claims.sourceSpan: set a penalty for pre-authorization defaults of at least $9,000 per violation and may not limit the base forfeiture to an amount less than 30 percent of the applicant's total support

claims.claim: The FCC may set the base forfeiture below 30% only by demonstrating that lower penalties are warranted in a particular instance. (core requirement, minus the qualifier)
claims.sourceSpan: unless the Commission demonstrates the need for lower penalties in a particular instance
claims.note: The case-by-case demonstration requirement to go below the 30% floor is faithful.

claims.claim: ...only by demonstrating IN WRITING that lower penalties are warranted...
claims.sourceSpan: unless the Commission demonstrates the need for lower penalties in a particular instance
claims.note: 'in writing' is a fabricated procedural qualifier. Neither 'writing'/'written' nor any filing/documentation formality for the lower-penalty demonstration appears anywhere in the source (verified: /in writing|written/ has zero hits). Source requires only that the Commission 'demonstrate the need for lower penalties in a particular instance.'

claims.claim: The penalty applies during the evaluation and pre-award phase, before an applicant begins receiving support.
claims.sourceSpan: Penalties for pre-authorization defaults.--In adopting rules for any new covered funding award
claims.note: Source uses the term 'pre-authorization defaults' but never defines it; 'evaluation and pre-award phase, before an applicant begins receiving support' is a reasonable plain-English inference, not stated. The analysis's own gaps[2] concedes the term is undefined.

claims.claim: Section 2 (new 254(m)(3)(B)(ii))
claims.sourceSpan: Evaluation of proposal.--The Commission shall evaluate a proposal described in subparagraph (B) against--
claims.note: Wrong statutory pincite. The compliance-history clause (ii) is nested under subparagraph (C) 'Evaluation of proposal'; subparagraph (B) 'Qualifications described' contains no clause (ii). Correct cite is 254(m)(3)(C)(ii), not (B)(ii).

claims.claim: The FCC must evaluate applicants against their history of compliance with not only FCC programs but also other government broadband deployment funding programs.
claims.sourceSpan: the applicant's history of complying with requirements in Commission and other government broadband deployment funding programs

claims.claim: ...administered by other federal agencies.
claims.sourceSpan: Commission and other government broadband deployment funding programs
claims.note: Source says 'other government' programs (broader - could include state/local); analysis narrows to 'other federal agencies', a qualifier not stated in source.

claims.claim: An applicant with unresolved compliance issues in another federal broadband program could be disqualified from FCC funding under this provision.
claims.sourceSpan: the applicant's history of complying with requirements in Commission and other government broadband deployment funding programs
claims.note: Source makes compliance history one evaluation factor; 'could be disqualified' is a plausible inference but the source does not state automatic disqualification.

claims.claim: The bill requires FCC to initiate rulemaking within 180 days but sets no deadline for completing or finalizing the rulemaking.
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this subsection, the Commission shall initiate a rulemaking proceeding
claims.note: Accurate: source imposes only an initiation deadline; no completion/finalization deadline present.

claims.claim: The vetting requirements apply only to applications submitted after rules are promulgated, leaving pending applications and existing commitments outside the new standards.
claims.sourceSpan: an award of covered funding that is made based on an application submitted to the Commission on or after the date on which rules are promulgated under paragraph (2)

claims.claim: The bill does not define what constitutes a pre-authorization default or how the $9,000 minimum penalty interacts with existing FCC forfeiture guidelines and statutory caps.
claims.sourceSpan: set a penalty for pre-authorization defaults of at least $9,000 per violation
claims.note: Accurate: term 'pre-authorization defaults' used but undefined; no interaction-with-existing-forfeiture language present.

claims.claim: FCC obligation to initiate rulemaking within 180 days to establish applicant vetting for high-cost USF broadband funding
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this subsection, the Commission shall initiate a rulemaking proceeding to establish a vetting process

claims.claim: Applicant documentation requirements: technical, financial, and operational capability evidence plus a reasonable business plan
claims.sourceSpan: technical, financial, and operational capabilities, and has a reasonable business plan

claims.claim: Compliance history review requirement covering FCC and other government broadband funding programs
claims.sourceSpan: the applicant's history of complying with requirements in Commission and other government broadband deployment funding programs

claims.claim: Minimum $9,000 per-violation penalty for pre-authorization defaults with a 30% of total support base forfeiture floor
claims.sourceSpan: set a penalty for pre-authorization defaults of at least $9,000 per violation and may not limit the base forfeiture to an amount less than 30 percent of the applicant's total support

claims.claim: High-cost USF award process - funds may only be awarded after applicants satisfy FCC-established vetting standards (applies to new applications after rules are finalized)
claims.sourceSpan: the Commission will only award covered funding to applicants that can demonstrate that they meet the qualifications

claims.claim: removed[] is empty - nothing is repealed.
claims.sourceSpan: amended by adding at the end the following
claims.note: Bill only ADDS new subsection (m); nothing is struck/repealed. Empty removed[] is faithful.

claims.claim: The rulemaking must be conducted 'consistent with principles of technology neutrality' - a substantive constraint on the FCC (cannot favor a particular technology) that appears nowhere in the analysis.
claims.sourceSpan: consistent with principles of technology neutrality, the Commission will only award covered funding to applicants
claims.note: 254(m)(3)(A) expressly binds the rulemaking to technology-neutrality principles. Not surfaced anywhere in summary/brief/top_lines/sections. Minor: a guiding principle rather than a core operative requirement.

notes: Source = enrolled Public Law 119-89 (S.98) text only; no referencedSources registered. Two material affirmative errors found: (1) sections[1].items[1].detail fabricates an 'in writing' requirement for the sub-30% demonstration (word absent from source); (2) underreported[0].section mis-pincites the compliance-history clause as 254(m)(3)(B)(ii) - it is (C)(ii). Remaining flags are minor (180-day 'establish' vs 'initiate rulemaking' compression in summary/brief; 'federal agencies' narrowing of 'other government'; pre-authorization phase gloss; disqualification inference). One omission: technology-neutrality constraint on the rulemaking. Featured quote is a Congressional Record floor statement not present in the fetched source, so unverifiable verbatim (not contradicted).
